title: Emergent induction in magnetic Weyl semimetals
abstract: We theoretically study emergent electromagnetic responses in Weyl semimetals. Focusing on magnetic Weyl semimetals, we develop a general theory of emergent induction driven by magnetic dynamics. We show that magnetoelectric (ME) responses in Weyl semimetals give rise to emergent induction mediated by magnetization dynamics. Using effective two-band models for magnetic Weyl semimetals, we derive a formula for the ME response that includes both intraband and interband contributions. The resulting formula shows that the intraband contribution is proportional to the relaxation time $τ$, whereas the interband contribution is associated with the separation of the Weyl nodes. Applying the general formula to a model of polar Weyl ferromagnets, we demonstrate that the dynamics of the toroidal moment is closely related to the emergent inductive response in polar Weyl ferromagnets, as recently discovered by Suzuki et al. [Y. Suzuki et al. arXiv:2607.12322]. The chemical-potential dependence of the inductance indicates that the emergent electromagnetic response is enhanced in the energy range of the Weyl dispersion, reflecting the topological nature of Weyl semimetals.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how magnetic dynamics induce an 'emergent induction' in Weyl semimetals. It derives the magnetoelectric response by separating contributions into intraband (dissipative) and interband (topological) parts. The key finding is that these systems inherently behave as emergent inductors due to strong magnetoelectric coupling, particularly when the chemical potential lies within the topological energy gap.
main_problem: The study investigates emergent electromagnetic responses, specifically 'emergent induction,' arising in magnetic Weyl semimetals due to underlying magnetic dynamics.
main_result: The magnetoelectric response is shown to have distinct intraband and interband contributions; the system generally acts as an emergent inductor due to this coupling.
method: Theoretical derivation using Boltzmann transport theory for intraband effects and the Kubo formula for interband contributions, applied to effective two-band models.
model_or_system: The physical system is a magnetic Weyl semimetal, modeled using effective two-band Hamiltonians that incorporate time-dependent magnetization acting as an emergent vector potential. The analysis applies this formalism to polar Weyl ferromagnets.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on separating the ME response into dissipative intraband and non-dissipative interband parts, and uses approximations regarding the relative magnitudes of different conductivity components in later sections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the chemical potential dependence of both the Fermi surface term ($\mathcal{C}_{O}$) and the interband effect term ($\mathcal{C}_I$), as well as the $\mu$ dependence of conductivity and inductance for specific models.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general theory by deriving ME responses from transport equations, separates contributions into intraband/interband terms, applies this to polar Weyl ferromagnets to calculate inductance components ($L_{	ext{long}}, L_{	ext{Hall}}$), and concludes with generalized expressions for the inductive response.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent induction mediated by topological band structures (Weyl nodes) provides a mechanism linking magnetism, topology, and macroscopic electromagnetic responses, which is relevant to advanced spintronic/topological materials research.
